content.text: The digital product economy is structurally unfair to creators in restricted markets. The tools that Western creators take for granted — Stripe for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-how-one-creator|payment]]s, Gumroad for storefront and delivery, PayPal for international transfers — are either unavailable or functionally broken for creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, and dozens of other markets. The answer is not finding a better platform. The answer is removing the platform layer entirely. A [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-digital-creators-explained-digital-creators|Sovereign Commerce]] digital commerce stack gives you a storefront you host, a payment processor that runs on blockchain rails, and an automated delivery system that sends your product within 30 seconds of payment confirmation. You collect revenue directly into a wallet you control. You convert to local currency through P2P exchanges at near-market rates. The platform cannot suspend you because you are not on any platform.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-3. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
